title: TGA home fieldwork guide: infiltration and run-off enquiry, with risk assessment
subject: Geography
unit: Summer 1: Physical fieldwork enquiry (Paper 1 Section B)
source: Written for geography/y10 lessons 63, 64 (TGA home fieldwork guide: infiltration and run-off enquiry, with risk assessment (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 63: Risk assessment, sampling and the fieldwork guide. A practical to do at home with an adult nearby. Read it all first.

practical.aim: To find out how surface type affects infiltration and run-off
equipment: An empty food tin with both ends removed (adult prepares; tape the edges)
safety: Adult prepares the tin; tape the edges; gloves
View any river only from a safe public point with an adult
An adult knows what you are doing and is nearby
Clear a space and tidy up afterwards; wash your hands
method: Mark 3 cm from the bottom of the tin
Choose four surface types (stratified) and three spots on each, 1 m apart (systematic)
Push the tin in evenly to the 3 cm mark
Pour 500 ml in steadily; start timing as you finish pouring
Stop when no water remains on the surface; record the time
On paving, pour 500 ml and observe where the run-off goes; take photos and a field sketch

questions.q: A risk assessment lists hazards and:
Big question: how could it go wrong and how do we stop it?
questions.a: Cuts, slips, germs, water: controlled by adults, taped tins, hand washing, staying out of rivers
